causal_analysis.observation: RS003 DL-04/Q-L-05 makes FORKED a derived state (|tips|>1) that only arises when a submitter declares intent (extend_leaf | fork_sibling) and the admission transaction's CAS (expected_tips_digest) passes; nothing today can push a branch into FORKED without a DECLARED intent attached to an admitted candidate.
causal_analysis.customer_wording_reading: CQ-1 says fork/merge 'should have a natural mechanism' ('должен быть естественный механизм') while describing duality as something 'we cannot avoid' -- this reads as a claim about the TREE'S PROPERTY (forking is a normal, expected, recurring shape of the data), not necessarily a claim that the SYSTEM must auto-detect forking without anyone declaring it. RS003's explicit-intent design already satisfies the weaker, more defensible reading: forking is natural in the sense that it is a first-class, repeatedly-occurring, non-exceptional state, not a rare error -- it just still requires an actor to say so.
causal_analysis.distinct_risk_if_misread: If the customer actually wants the STRONGER reading -- the system itself notices that two independently-admitted, intent-less refinements have drifted into semantic conflict and marks the branch FORKED on its own -- that is a different, substantially riskier mechanism: it needs a conflict-detection CRITERION (textual diff? keyword overlap? an explicit `contradicts` relation some reviewer must have created? LLM judgement?) and an owner for false positives (branch wrongly marked FORKED, blocking downstream consumers) and false negatives (real semantic fork never detected, silently returns one tip as if uncontested).
causal_analysis.position: Both readings are defensible from the quote alone; RS003 only designed for the weaker one. This is exactly the kind of ambiguity the card's task 1 flags and the correct response is a precise question to the customer via RS004, not a silent choice either way.

causal_analysis.observation: F1/F2 confirmed: record_id is global, AA/AB are visibility scopes. F3's risk requires a scope rule that does not exist yet because the similarity feature itself does not exist yet (RS003 left keyword location as NU-01, OPEN).
causal_analysis.customer_wording_reading: CQ-2 explicitly asks two DIFFERENT things in one breath: (a) whether branches AA/AB being 'different but possibly similar' changes uniqueness rules (answered by F1/F2: no, uniqueness is mechanical and branch-independent), and (b) whether keywords build a similarity GRAPH scoped to 'the branches of a tree grown from a single root' -- i.e. is similarity meant to stay WITHIN one family_id (one tree) by design, or can it legitimately cross family_id boundaries (different trees, possibly unrelated roots)?
causal_analysis.gap_in_RS003: RS003 Q-L-11 (answers_11_14.json) commits to 'suggestions/counts do not disclose hidden state' as a GENERAL scope-safety principle (the same Q-L-09/10 ScopedView-first discipline), but never states the family_id boundary question CQ-2 asks literally. A similarity graph that is scope-safe (never reveals existence across grants) can still legitimately be asked to operate either within one family or across many; RS003 did not pick either, because the keyword LOCATION itself (NU-01) was never decided.
causal_analysis.position: F3 is a correct, not-yet-mitigated risk description, but it conflates two separable concerns that RS004 must keep apart: (1) visibility-scope safety (must never leak existence across GRANTS -- already covered by the existing Q-L-09/10 ScopedView discipline and TD-DOM-19 closure) and (2) tree-scope policy (should similarity be restricted to one family_id as a matter of PRODUCT DESIGN, independent of who can see what). A caller who is independently granted visibility into two different family_id trees should get a well-defined answer either way; today neither axis is decided.

causal_analysis.observation: F4/F5 independently confirmed. omh_todo gives DOM nothing stable to key against externally: position is mutable across any `set`, and the only guard (item_text prefix) protects omh_todo's OWN advance call, not a third party's stored reference.
causal_analysis.customer_wording_reading: CQ-3 asks, almost word for word, for exactly this mechanism: 'how is the item stored in the plan, so that if the plan is updated and the item seems to have changed, but the claim references it by number or id without specifying the text or a reference -- that reference is not individual' -- and concludes 'if it is done by eye [without a form], consider that this will work only sometimes, if at all -- agreed?' The customer has already correctly derived F4/F5 from intuition; the analyst's job is to turn this into an exact engineering requirement and a verification plan, not to re-derive what the customer already said.

what_the_claim_must_store_at_creation: plan_item_snapshot: {source: 'omh_todo', session_ref_or_home_scope, captured_at (server time), item_text_verbatim (full text, not a prefix), item_text_sha256, phase (if present), position_at_capture (int, informational only, NEVER used alone as identity)}

No DOM field may be 'the item number' alone: that reproduces exactly the omh_todo advance-path weakness (F4) one layer up, because DOM has no more claim to item-identity stability than omh_todo's own advance call does.
when_a_pin_must_be_detected_as_stale: On revalidation, DOM must re-read the live omh_todo record (via action=show/recall) and compare item_text_sha256 against the CURRENT text at the position the claim remembers; a mismatch at that position, a `set` that removed/renamed the item (no item at that position still starts with the stored prefix), or inability to read the record at all (session cleared / home not found) are ALL pin_behind, following the existing VersionPin/RevisionPin strict-default pattern (RS003 Q-L-08) rather than silently falling back to 'closest by number'.

A `set` write is uniquely dangerous because it 'drops items left out' with NO history (F4) -- so DOM's pin must not assume the item still exists at all once it detects any discrepancy; it must surface UNVERIFIABLE_IN_SCOPE-style explicit unresolved state (same vocabulary RS003 already uses for cross-branch pins), not guess.

causal_analysis.position: RS004 should design this as the SAME pin-and-stale-detection pattern RS003 already built for VersionPin/RevisionPin/QuotePin (Q-L-04/08), reusing SOURCE_BYTES_MISMATCH's precedent of 'DOM keeps its own immutable copy and re-compares' rather than inventing a new mechanism, and should not assume OMH will ever grow a stable per-item ID -- today's todo_store.py gives none and nothing in the card or in omh_todo's own tool schema promises one is coming.

causal_analysis.observation: projections.py:46 confirms today's 'converge' really is a bare boolean latch ('elif kind=='converge': converged=True'), matching TD-DOM-18 (confirmed open/major in tech_debt.md:24: 'одно событие converge снимает BRANCH_NOT_CONVERGED навсегда, включая ревизии, добавленные после решения'). RS003 DL-08/Q-L-07 already designed a replacement: a converge EVENT carrying a revision vector, a criteria_digest, a subject, and supersedes-chaining to the prior converge event.
causal_analysis.orchestrator_minimum_vs_DL-08: The orchestrator's card (task 4) describes a minimum of 'pairs of record_id, a closed reason code, who decided, basis' for the customer's agreed-but-unspecified convergence form. Read literally, a PAIR of record_id describes a two-endpoint relationship -- which is the shape of RS003's `merges` relation (Q-L-05/Q-L-06: claim_version(merge) -> claim_version(tip), same family) for resolving a SPECIFIC fork between TWO tips -- not the shape of DL-08's branch-level `converged` axis, which is about a WHOLE BRANCH's criteria coverage against a VECTOR of dependency revisions, not a pair.
causal_analysis.position: These are two legitimately different mechanisms already distinguished in RS003's own model (Q-L-05 vs Q-L-07/DL-08) and the card's 'minimum' risks collapsing them into one weaker form that loses DL-08's vector+criteria_digest+supersedes fields for the branch-level case, while also under-specifying the merges relation for the multi-tip case (a fork can have MORE than two concurrent tips -- RS003 explicitly allows |tips|>1, not just 2 -- so a fixed 'pair of record_id' cannot represent an n-way merge). The task's own instruction ('не предлагать слабее уже спроектированного') is violated if RS004 adopts the two-field minimum as-is for EITHER mechanism without at minimum carrying forward DL-08's fields for the branch axis and allowing >2 endpoints for the tips-merge relation.
